items.headline: Martine Rose takes over Balenciaga
items.caption: The British designer replaces Pierpaolo Piccioli a day after he left.
body: Rose already advised on Balenciaga's menswear before.
Highsnobiety calls it a recentring for the house.
Watch for: sharper, street-smart menswear.

items.headline: Nike Air Max 95s in Italian leather
items.caption: One Block Down's 'Lux' pairs come in four Italy-inspired colours.
body: The leather is finished in Italy; the rest is made in Vietnam.
It's the classic runner made luxe.
How to wear it: with tailored trousers.

items.headline: Jordan's fuzzy green dad shoe
items.caption: The DMSN 95 'Green Noise' mixes patent leather and hairy suede.
body: It looks Bottega Veneta-inspired, minus the price.
The dadcore shape is all green.
How to wear it: with navy or grey, nothing else loud.

items.headline: Bottega Veneta does Moomin
items.caption: The Finnish cartoon gets Bottega's leathercraft treatment.
body: Highsnobiety says it feels natural, not forced.
It shows how to do a character-luxury collab right.
How to wear it: one playful piece, rest plain.

items.headline: A Travis Scott GTA 6 sneaker, before the game
items.caption: Nike Air Force 1s tied to Rockstar's long-awaited game.
body: GTA 6 finally launches on 19 November.
A black pair has pink stars and a backwards Swoosh.
Fair warning: they may be harder to get than the game.

items.headline: The 2027 Met Gala celebrates T-shirts and jeans
items.caption: 'extraORDINARY' looks at how designers elevate everyday clothes.
body: It replaces a cancelled John Galliano show.
GQ says it's great news for men.
How to wear it: a perfect white tee and dark denim.

items.headline: Levi's wants slim jeans back
items.caption: The 518 Slim sits between skinny and baggy.
body: It takes ideas from early-2000s skate and indie style.
GQ says it's a good middle ground.
How to wear it: with chunky trainers and a bomber.

items.headline: Best-dressed men at Chanel's Sydney show
items.caption: Chanel's Cruise 26-27 show came to Barangaroo's Cutaway.
body: Joel Edgerton, Baz Luhrmann and Dom Dolla sat front row.
Matthieu Blazy's Chanel is now dressing men too.
Style lesson: relaxed tailoring, no tie.

items.headline: Seized Rolexes from a money-laundering case go to auction
items.caption: 53 lots from Singapore's £1.7 billion case are up for sale.
body: They include a green Submariner and a white-gold Nautilus.
Hotlotz sells them online from 9 to 29 November.
Style lesson: buy the watch, skip the backstory.

items.headline: Desert boots that can handle winter
items.caption: Esquire picks seven chukkas built for wet weather.
body: They're lighter than heavy winter boots.
Better than dress shoes on slushy streets.
How to wear it: with chinos or dark jeans.

items.headline: One-of-a-kind watches for charity
items.caption: 21 unique watches go under the hammer for ELA at Christie's.
body: Proceeds fund research into rare brain diseases called leukodystrophies.
The sale is on 9 November in Geneva.
The first sale in 2024 raised close to $1 million.

items.headline: The public helped buy an 800-year-old estate for wildlife
items.caption: Donors worldwide raised millions to buy Northumberland's Rothbury Estate.
body: Curlews, lapwings and rare bumblebees live there.
David Attenborough cheered the result.

items.headline: A man spent 12 days returning a worker's lost salary
items.caption: Pedro Moro found a month's pay lying in a Brazilian plaza.
body: The money belonged to a young builder saving for his daughter.
Moro tracked him down and gave it all back.

items.headline: A 'possibly extinct' slow loris was here all along
items.caption: The Bangka slow loris was last documented by scientists in the 1930s.
body: A local group on Bangka island has been rescuing and releasing them for years.
In 2015 it was listed as possibly extinct.
